Installation on Windows, macOS and Linux

Source: vignettes/articles/installation.Rmd
installation.Rmd

MERIDIAN requires R 4.3.0 or later. RStudio is recommended. The package is installed from GitHub as source code, so its C++ code needs the appropriate compiler even when dependencies are available as binaries.

Windows

  1. Install R for Windows.
  2. Install RStudio and Rtools matching your R release. Use the default Rtools installation location, then restart RStudio.
  3. Run the R installation commands below.

Rtools includes the C/C++ tools needed to compile MERIDIAN. Available CRAN Windows binaries can be used for dependencies. If R cannot find the compiler, check the installation with:

install.packages("pkgbuild")
pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)

macOS

Install the CRAN version of R and RStudio for your processor architecture: Apple Silicon or Intel. Install Apple’s Command Line Tools from Terminal:

xcode-select --install

Then run the R installation commands below. Use available CRAN binaries for dependencies. If a dependency needs compilation with Fortran, use the compiler matching the installed R build from the official R for macOS tools page. Avoid mixing Intel and Apple Silicon libraries in one R installation.

Linux

On Ubuntu or Debian, run these commands in a terminal before installing the R package:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential r-base-dev cmake libuv1-dev \
  libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev \
  libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev libpng-dev libjpeg-dev libtiff-dev libwebp-dev libx11-dev

For other distributions or current dependency requirements, inspect the plan in R:

pak::pkg_sysreqs("SalvaOsuna/MERIDIAN")

If fs fails with libuv was not found, install the libuv development package (libuv1-dev on Ubuntu/Debian) before retrying. A dependency build failure means MERIDIAN may not yet be installed.

Install and launch on any supported system

Run in the R console:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("SalvaOsuna/MERIDIAN")
MERIDIAN::run_app()

To update, restart R first, then run:

pak::pkg_install("SalvaOsuna/MERIDIAN", upgrade = TRUE)
MERIDIAN::run_app()

The bundled example works offline. A browser can use a system font when Google Fonts is unavailable. NASA POWER weather retrieval requires internet access; uploaded environmental covariates remain available if retrieval fails.

Reports and optional tools

  • HTML reports: Pandoc, provided with RStudio or installed separately.
  • PDF reports: Pandoc, the R package pagedown, and Chrome, Chromium or Edge. A LaTeX installation is not needed for this export route.
  • Tables and individual figures: CSV/Excel and PNG/SVG/TIFF/PDF exports are available from the Reports module. Individual PDF figures do not need the browser-based report exporter.
install.packages("pagedown")
pagedown::find_chrome()

If Pandoc is not detected, run the app from RStudio or put a standalone Pandoc installation on the system PATH. RStudio’s direct and architecture-specific bundled locations are checked by the report exporter.

Local development

Install development dependencies and load the source project:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
source("run_app_dev.R")

After copying a checkout between operating systems, remove old compiled files before loading it:

pkgbuild::clean_dll(".")
source("run_app_dev.R")

The automated workflow builds, tests and starts the installed app on Linux, Windows and macOS. The local checkout can only exercise the system on which it is running; consult GitHub Actions for the latest results on the other systems.
